_comment: Textové profily coinů: k čemu je coin zamýšlen a jestli to naše měření potvrzuje. Klíč je CoinGecko id. Generuje tool/build_profiles.dart, který deklaraci projektu konfrontuje s naměřenými čísly - proto to není převyprávěný marketingový popis. Pole "evidence" říká, jak je odstavec podložený: documented (popis i měření), thin (jedno z toho), none (nic, text pak jen konstatuje, že informace nejsou dostupné). Ruční úprava textu je v pořádku a přežije, dokud profil nezestárne nad --max-age.

avalanche-2.purpose: A smart contract platform whose distinguishing idea is subnets, letting an institution or a game run a chain with its own rules while still settling to the main network. That has drawn enterprise and gaming projects more than retail DeFi. In its segment it sits mid-field, with $476M of locked value and $1.5B of stablecoins issued, an order of magnitude below Solana but ahead of most. Development is steady at 60 commits in four weeks from 219 contributors, and the community remains large at 496k watchlists.

binancecoin.purpose: The native token of Binance, the largest exchange, where it pays fee discounts, and the gas token of BNB Chain, where it pays for transactions. That dual role is unusual and it works. BNB Chain holds $5.4B of locked value and $13.9B of issued stablecoins, third among all chains we track, behind only Ethereum and Tron, while scheduled burns shrink the supply over time. Its long-term price record is the strongest we measure at 100% a year since 2017, though it follows the exchange as much as the chain.

bitcoin.purpose: Digital gold: the original cryptocurrency and still the reference asset the rest of the market is priced against, held as a long-term store of value rather than spent. It leads its segment on every measure we have, first in market capitalisation, first in trading volume, and first in search interest across roughly 8000 coins. The fundamentals behind it are the strongest here as well, with 303 commits in the last four weeks from 342 contributors, the widest development base we track anywhere. The 21 million cap has never moved.

bitcoin-cash.purpose: A 2017 fork of Bitcoin that raised the block size so the coin would stay cheap to spend, taking the side of payments over store of value. The market rather than the debate settled which way that went. Within the payments segment it now sits far behind, with $42k of locked value and no commits on the node in the last four weeks. Real liquidity and name recognition remain, twenty-ninth in search interest, but the price has returned 2% a year since 2019 against Bitcoin's 38%.

cardano.purpose: A smart contract platform distinguished by process rather than by product: every major change is peer-reviewed before it ships, which has made development careful and slow. In its own segment it sits well behind the leaders, with $61.7M of locked value and $65.2M of stablecoins against Ethereum's billions, on $38k of protocol revenue over thirty days. What it does have is one of the largest and most durable communities on our list at 963k watchlists, and steady development at 67 commits in four weeks.

chainlink.purpose: The standard oracle network and the dominant one by a wide margin. Blockchains cannot read anything outside themselves, so Chainlink pays independent node operators to fetch prices and other external data and agree on a single answer contracts can rely on, with LINK paying those operators and staked as collateral they lose for reporting badly. Chain-level metrics do not apply to infrastructure like this. What does apply is its reach across dozens of chains, an active codebase at 162 commits in four weeks, and eighth place in search interest.

dogecoin.purpose: The original meme coin and still the largest, a 2013 Litecoin fork made as a parody, with one-minute blocks, tiny fees, and a supply that grows forever. It states no utility, so attention and liquidity are the whole story, and by that measure it leads its segment comfortably: 875k watchlists and eleventh place in search interest across roughly 8000 coins. Development has all but stopped at 1 commit in four weeks. The price has still compounded 55% a year since 2019, carried by recognition rather than use.

ethereum.purpose: The dominant smart contract platform, and the chain most of decentralised finance actually runs on. Where Bitcoin stores value, Ethereum executes code that anyone can deploy, with ETH paying for the computation. Its lead in its own segment is not close: $48.8B of locked value and $147.9B of stablecoins issued on the chain, both several times any competitor we track. Development is broad and steady across 444 contributors, and the community is the second largest on our list. The price has compounded 26% a year since 2017.

hedera-hashgraph.purpose: An enterprise ledger governed by a council of large corporations including Google, IBM, Boeing and Deutsche Telekom rather than by token holders, selling timestamping and ordered consensus as an auditable service that business systems can log events to. It competes for corporate blockchain work rather than for open finance, a segment where adoption is slow and largely private. The public figures stay small: $26.1M of locked value, $30.3M of stablecoins, and $313k of protocol revenue over a year. No public code repository is linked, so development is not measured.

litecoin.purpose: One of the oldest cryptocurrencies still running, a 2011 Bitcoin fork with four times faster blocks and an 84 million cap, built for smaller everyday payments. It has worked exactly as designed for fourteen years, which is also its difficulty: newer chains cover the same ground more cheaply, and we record only $774k of locked value and $11k of protocol revenue over thirty days. Recognition and liquidity remain, twenty-sixth in search interest, but the price is down 19% a year since 2017.

monero.purpose: The other established privacy coin, and the stricter of the two: where comparable systems make shielding optional, every Monero transaction conceals sender, receiver, and amount by default. That has made it the practical standard for people who need financial privacy, and it also means almost nothing about its usage is measurable from outside. What is measurable is the project itself, and it is healthy, with 197 commits in four weeks from 341 contributors. It ranks fifteenth by market capitalisation while sitting only 265th in search interest.

ripple.purpose: A settlement network aimed squarely at cross-border banking, where XRP acts as a bridge asset so neither institution has to pre-fund an account abroad. Transfers finalise in seconds and the ledger has run without interruption since 2012. In the payments segment it is the best known name and fourth in search interest across roughly 8000 coins, though its measurable on-chain footprint stays modest at $41M of locked value and $1.0B of stablecoins. Development is active, 120 commits in four weeks from 170 contributors.

shiba-inu.purpose: The second largest meme coin, launched on Ethereum and carried by an unusually large and organised community. Unlike Dogecoin it has claimed to grow into a working financial network with its own exchange and its own layer 2, Shibarium, but none of that appears in what we measure: no locked value, no protocol revenue, and no public code repository. Within its own segment it holds second place on attention alone, 818k watchlists, while the price is down 21% a year since 2021.

solana.purpose: The strongest challenger to Ethereum among smart contract platforms, built for speed: one unified ledger, parallel execution, sub-second finality, and fees measured in fractions of a cent. It sits second in its segment on the numbers that matter, $5.8B locked and $15.7B of stablecoins issued, and second only to Tron on protocol revenue at $21.8M in thirty days. Development is the most intense on our list at 371 commits in four weeks. Its weak point has been network reliability, and volatility remains high.

stellar.purpose: A payment network built around the currency-exchange problem: regulated entities called anchors hold real deposits and issue matching credits, and XLM bridges between them so a transfer can cross currencies in seconds. It shares the cross-border payments segment with XRP and sits second there, with $234M of locked value and $866M of stablecoins issued, meaningful figures for a payment rail. Its focus is remittances and tokenised assets rather than DeFi. Development is quiet at 24 commits in four weeks.

sui.purpose: A newer smart contract platform from former Meta engineers, built on an object-centric data model that lets unrelated transactions execute in parallel, with the Move language handling assets safely by design. For a chain listed only in 2023 it has established itself quickly: $445M of locked value, $399M of stablecoins issued, and the busiest young codebase on our list at 155 commits in four weeks from 409 contributors. Interest runs ahead of size, thirteenth in search against thirty-third by market capitalisation.

the-open-network.purpose: A general-purpose chain originally designed at Telegram and now developed independently, built for very cheap transfers at messenger scale and reaching users through wallet integration rather than through exchanges. Among smart contract platforms it is a mid-sized player: $49.9M of locked value, $757M of stablecoins issued, and $2.4M of protocol revenue over the past year. Development continues at 38 commits in four weeks, though from a narrow base of 66 contributors. We hold no price history for it, so its long-term record is missing from the score.

tron.purpose: The main settlement rail for stablecoin transfers, above all USDT, where fees low enough for small remittances have made it a default across Asia and Latin America. In that niche it dominates: $93.7B of stablecoins issued on the chain, second only to Ethereum, and $362M of protocol revenue over the past year, the highest figure of any project we track. The tradeoff is decentralisation, with 27 elected validators and only 6 commits on the node in four weeks. It is used far more heavily than it is discussed.

uniswap.purpose: The dominant decentralised exchange and the protocol that made automated market making the standard design: pooled assets priced by formula instead of an order book, running without an operator. It leads the DEX segment by trading volume across the chains it is deployed on. UNI itself is the governance token, so holders vote on the treasury and on upgrades rather than collecting the trading fees, which is worth knowing before reading anything into its price. Chain-level metrics do not apply to a protocol, and our own DEX volume figure is missing.

zcash.purpose: One of the two established privacy coins, and the one built on zero-knowledge proofs: a transaction can be verified without revealing sender, receiver, or amount, under the same 21 million cap as Bitcoin. By design most of its usage cannot be measured from outside, so the segment is judged on standing and on development instead. Both are strong here, with 223 commits in four weeks and sixth place in search interest across roughly 8000 coins, well above its eleventh place by market capitalisation.

near.purpose: A sharded smart-contract chain whose current emphasis is chain abstraction: a NEAR account and its contracts can sign transactions on other networks, while NEAR itself executes applications. That makes it a general-purpose platform rather than an AI product on its own. It is a mid-sized chain in this list, with $118M locked and $104M of stablecoins issued, at market-cap rank thirty-six. Development is active at 130 commits from 246 contributors in four weeks, and its 334k watchlists show much more attention than a small chain.

tether-gold.purpose: A tokenised-gold product: each XAUt represents ownership of one fine troy ounce on an allocated physical gold bar, rather than a chain or a protocol with its own network activity. Its job is to make that claim transferable on public blockchains. At market-cap rank thirty-eight and with $286M of daily volume, it is one of the larger tokenised-gold instruments in this list, though only 34k users watch it. Our pipeline records $3.9M of annual protocol revenue but no public code repository or chain metrics, so it cannot test the backing itself.

ripple-usd.purpose: A dollar stablecoin issued by Ripple for payments and settlement, redeemable one-for-one against segregated cash and cash-equivalent reserves. It is native to XRP Ledger and Ethereum, so its purpose is price stability for transfers rather than price exposure to a network. It has already reached market-cap rank forty-one and $136M of daily volume, but its attention remains modest at rank 715 and 16k watchlists. Our snapshot carries no reserve, code, or chain-usage measure for the token, so the data confirms distribution and liquidity, not the issuer's reserve claim.

bittensor.purpose: A blockchain-coordinated market for machine-learning services, where independent subnets supply work such as inference or storage and validators score it; TAO rewards the participants and secures the network. It competes in AI and infrastructure rather than in ordinary DeFi. The measurable chain footprint is still limited at $46M locked, but the project is unusually visible for its size: market-cap rank forty-four versus search rank twenty-four. Its codebase is active at 149 commits from 86 contributors in four weeks, while 199k watchlists show a sizable interested audience.

aave.purpose: A decentralised lending market: suppliers place assets in pools and borrowers post collateral, while AAVE governs changes to the protocol. It competes with other on-chain credit protocols, where fees and revenue matter more than a chain's TVL. Our snapshot records $81k of revenue over thirty days and $1.6M over a year, plus two audits on record, but no comparable protocol TVL. The linked V3 repository had no commits in the last four weeks, although it has 19 contributors; that is a narrow development signal rather than evidence that the wider protocol has stopped.

aster-2.purpose: A decentralised perpetuals exchange, with an order-book mode for derivatives trading across BNB Chain, Ethereum, Solana, and Arbitrum. ASTER is the token attached to that venue rather than a base-layer coin. The available measurements do not record the exchange's fees, revenue, or DEX volume, so they cannot establish its position among perpetuals venues. They do show real market attention: $192M of daily token volume and search rank twenty-one. The linked documentation repository logged four commits from eleven contributors in four weeks, a modest but current public development signal.

pax-gold.purpose: A tokenised-gold claim issued by Paxos: one PAXG represents one fine troy ounce of allocated London Good Delivery gold, which makes fractional ownership and on-chain transfer possible. It belongs with real-world asset tokens, not smart-contract platforms. At market-cap rank forty-seven and with $186M of daily volume, it is a large instrument in this dataset, though search interest is only 172nd and 46k users watch it. The public contract repository has no recent commits; our data has no reserve measurement, so it cannot independently verify the allocated-gold claim.

world-liberty-financial.purpose: The governance token of World Liberty Financial: its stated role is voting on the direction of the WLF protocol, not ownership, dividends, or a claim on company assets. That places it among governance tokens linked to DeFi and the USD1 stablecoin rather than among payment coins. The project has market-cap rank forty-nine, and our pipeline records $10.5M of protocol revenue in thirty days and $120.6M in a year. There is no public code repository in the snapshot, so those figures show recorded activity but do not let us assess the protocol's implementation or decentralisation.

ondo-finance.purpose: A governance token for the Ondo DAO, whose documented remit includes Flux Finance, a lending market that accepts tokenised securities as collateral. It therefore sits in real-world-asset DeFi, not as a token that directly represents those securities. The linked public repository is explicitly a one-time code snapshot and its last push was in 2022, so its lack of recent commits says little about current development. Our pipeline records no protocol revenue or TVL for Ondo itself; the strongest measurable signal is its 222k watchlists despite search rank 103.

morpho.purpose: An open lending infrastructure built around isolated markets, where borrowers post collateral and lenders can use vaults whose curators allocate capital across markets. MORPHO governs this credit layer rather than a chain. The design gives each market its own oracle, collateral, and risk parameters instead of pooling all risk together. Our snapshot does not record Morpho revenue, TVL, audits, or a public code repository, so it cannot judge lending scale or implementation activity. It does show a $1.7B market capitalisation, search rank seventy-one, and comparatively limited attention at 22k watchlists.

pump-fun.purpose: The token associated with Pump.fun, a Solana launchpad for creating and trading new tokens, especially meme coins. That makes it an exchange and issuance venue token rather than a meme coin with a standalone use case. Its market measures show attention and liquidity rather than platform use: market-cap rank fifty-two, $217M of daily volume, and nineteenth place in search interest. The snapshot has no project description, code repository, DEX volume, or protocol revenue, so it cannot test how much of the launchpad's activity accrues to PUMP or its token holders.

ethena.purpose: Ethena's governance token, used to vote on critical protocol decisions and to elect risk-committee members; it is not the dollar-linked asset the protocol issues. It belongs with stablecoin and DeFi governance rather than with payment tokens. The snapshot records no revenue, TVL, reserve data, code repository, or audits for the protocol, so it cannot measure its stablecoin operation or governance quality. What it does record is substantial token liquidity at $715M a day, while search interest is only 270th and 114k users keep it on watchlists.

sky.purpose: The governance token of Sky Protocol, the renamed and upgraded Maker protocol, where token holders govern a system built around the USDS stablecoin. Its function is protocol control rather than a direct claim on the stablecoin's dollar reserves. The dataset offers little evidence for how that system is performing: it records no revenue, TVL, audits, or public repository. Market attention is also limited for a token at market-cap rank fifty-four, with $10.5M of daily volume, search rank ninety, and fewer than 10k watchlists. The summary therefore confirms the role but not the protocol's operating scale.

pepe.purpose: A meme token built around Pepe the Frog, with no stated operating service beyond the culture and attention attached to the meme. That makes attention and liquidity the meaningful measures, not TVL or protocol revenue. By those measures it is one of the largest meme coins in this list: market-cap rank fifty-five, search rank fourteen, 394k watchlists, and $315M of daily volume. There is no public repository or on-chain business metric in the snapshot. Its use case is therefore community recognition, while the data cannot show recurring usage beyond trading interest.

polkadot.purpose: A multichain security and interoperability network: specialised parachains connect to the relay chain, inherit its validator security, and exchange messages through XCM. DOT is used for network governance, staking, and access to core computation. The snapshot does not attribute chain TVL, stablecoins, or revenue to Polkadot, so it cannot measure adoption of that model directly. It does show a durable developer base of 90 commits from 382 contributors in four weeks and a large community at 636k watchlists. Its search rank of fifty-five closely matches market-cap rank fifty-six.

worldcoin-wld.purpose: The governance token connected to World ID and World Chain. World ID lets a person prove they are unique online through privacy-preserving proofs, with Orb verification providing its highest-assurance credential; WLD is not itself that identity proof. The associated chain remains small in the platform segment, with $33M locked and $17M of issued stablecoins at market-cap rank sixty. No public repository is linked in the snapshot, so development is not measured. Interest is middling as well, with search rank 104 and 102k watchlists.

internet-computer.purpose: A smart-contract platform that treats applications as canisters: WebAssembly code and persistent state executed and replicated by network subnets. Its ambition is to provide application hosting as well as ordinary blockchain transactions. In the platform segment, the measurable footprint is small at $14.5M locked and $3.9M of stablecoins issued, despite market-cap rank sixty-one. Development is unusually active at 298 commits from 159 contributors in four weeks. The contrast supports the project's technical activity, but not broad financial use of the chain.

bfusd.purpose: A Binance reward-bearing asset redeemable for a dollar stablecoin and usable as margin in a futures account, so its role is collateral plus account rewards rather than an independent payment network. Its almost flat price history is consistent with that design. It has reached market-cap rank sixty-four, but the public interest around it is thin: search rank 900 and only 414 watchlists, with $5.1M of daily volume. The snapshot has no code repository, reserve data, audit record, or chain metrics, so it cannot independently assess the reward mechanism or the redemption backing.

united-stables.purpose: A dollar-stablecoin listing for which the available project material supplies no stated purpose, reserve explanation, or public code repository. The nearly flat price history is compatible with a stablecoin, but it does not verify a peg or the assets behind it. Its market-cap rank is sixty-five and daily volume is $209M, while search rank 861 and 473 watchlists show very little public attention. Those figures establish exchange liquidity, not how the token is issued, redeemed, governed, or backed; the summary should remain deliberately limited until better primary material is available.

lighter.purpose: A decentralised derivatives venue whose stated technical distinction is verifiable order matching and liquidations, aimed at perpetual trading with exchange-like performance. LIT is therefore tied to a trading platform, not a base-layer network. The snapshot records no DEX volume, fees, revenue, audit, or public repository, so it cannot compare the venue's actual trading activity with other perpetual exchanges. It does show liquid token markets at $197M a day and search rank thirty-nine, although only 20k users have it on watchlists. The role is documented; the operating evidence is still thin.

ethereum-classic.purpose: The original Ethereum chain that retained proof-of-work after Ethereum moved to proof-of-stake. It remains a permissionless smart-contract platform, with ETC paying for execution and mining securing the ledger. Its platform use is very small in this dataset at $77k locked and $74k of stablecoins, despite market-cap rank sixty-nine. The linked public site recorded eight commits from 102 contributors in four weeks, while attention is limited at search rank 143. It preserves a distinct consensus model, but our metrics show little DeFi activity on the chain.

polygon-ecosystem-token.purpose: The native token replacing MATIC in Polygon's Ethereum-scaling network. POL pays gas on Polygon PoS and is staked by validators, while the wider project aims to connect multiple chains around Ethereum. The chain is substantial in its segment, with $812M locked and $3.1B of issued stablecoins, although well behind Ethereum and the largest alternative platforms. It has strong public interest at search rank twenty-seven and 664k watchlists. No public repository is linked in this snapshot, so development activity is not measured here.

quant-network.purpose: The token used around Quant's Overledger platform, a service for building applications that connect more than one distributed-ledger network through a common interface. It belongs to interoperability infrastructure rather than to a chain with native DeFi. The snapshot records no chain TVL, protocol revenue, public repository, or audits, so it cannot measure whether the platform is being used by the applications it targets. QNT still has market-cap rank seventy-four and 132k watchlists, but search interest is only 721st, showing a specialised rather than broad retail audience.

just.purpose: The governance token of JUST, a TRON-based DeFi system built around the USDJ stablecoin and collateralised lending. JST is therefore a protocol-control token, not the stablecoin itself or TRON's native payment coin. Our snapshot has no linked repository, revenue, TVL, audit, or DEX-volume figure for the protocol, leaving its operating scale unmeasured. It ranks seventy-six by market capitalisation but has only 16k watchlists and search rank 268. The role is documented, while the evidence for current use is thin.

arbitrum.purpose: An Ethereum layer-two rollup that executes transactions away from Ethereum and posts their results back to it; ARB governs parts of that network rather than paying ordinary transaction fees. It is one of the larger smart-contract platforms in the snapshot, with $1.4B locked and $3.2B of issued stablecoins. Development is visible but quiet in the linked documentation repository at three commits from 26 contributors in four weeks. Search rank twenty-two and 212k watchlists show that its market attention runs ahead of its rank seventy-eight by capitalisation.

nexo.purpose: The token associated with Nexo's centrally operated crypto-finance service, whose products include lending, borrowing, and account rewards. It should be judged as a platform token rather than as a decentralised lending protocol, because its business activity does not appear as chain TVL or protocol fees. The snapshot records no public repository, audits, or operating metric, only market signals: rank eighty by capitalisation, $4.5M of daily volume, and 49k watchlists. Its documented role is clear, but this dataset cannot independently assess the service behind it.

algorand.purpose: A general-purpose layer-one blockchain secured by pure proof of stake, where stake-weighted participants form the consensus committees and ALGO pays for network activity. Its technical focus is a fast base layer rather than a single DeFi application. The measurable financial footprint is small at $30M locked and $37M of stablecoins despite market-cap rank eighty-one. Development remains active at 33 commits from 114 contributors in four weeks, and 291k watchlists exceed its search rank of 161. The project is maintained, but the snapshot does not show broad on-chain capital use.

cosmos.purpose: The token of the Cosmos Hub, which coordinates an interchain built around IBC messaging and can extend its validator security to consumer chains. ATOM is used for staking and governance of that hub; it is not a claim on every independent chain built with the Cosmos SDK. Our snapshot attributes only $110k of TVL to the Hub and no stablecoin issuance or revenue, so it does not demonstrate economic activity across the broader interchain. The linked repository is an old wallet project, making its zero recent commits unsuitable as a development measure. Community interest remains substantial at 335k watchlists.

render-token.purpose: A token for the Render Network, which coordinates access to distributed GPU rendering and computing capacity rather than running a general-purpose financial chain. Its usefulness depends on work being supplied and completed by that network, not on chain TVL. The snapshot has no revenue, usage, public-repository, or audit measure for that activity, so it cannot verify demand for GPU jobs. It holds market-cap rank eighty-seven, with 257k watchlists and search rank 115, showing strong recognition but not measured network utilisation.

dash.purpose: A proof-of-work payment network that adds collateralised masternodes for services and governance alongside miners. DASH is intended for direct transfers, so payment activity and liquidity matter more than DeFi TVL. The snapshot records only $95k locked and no stablecoins or protocol revenue, which points to a small on-chain finance footprint. Development on the linked Tenderdash repository is active at 36 commits from 269 contributors in four weeks. Attention remains high for its size, with search rank thirty-three and 101k watchlists, but the data does not measure real payment volume.

jupiter-exchange-solana.purpose: The governance token of Jupiter, a Solana trading venue and swap aggregator that routes orders across liquidity sources. It belongs with decentralised exchanges, where fees and revenue are more useful than a chain's TVL. The pipeline records $3.5M of revenue in thirty days and $34.5M in a year, a meaningful operating signal for this segment, though its own DEX-volume field is missing. JUP ranks eighty-nine by capitalisation, has search rank sixty-four, and 137k watchlists. No public repository is linked, so development is not measured.

pancakeswap-token.purpose: The governance and incentive token of PancakeSwap, a decentralised exchange that uses automated market-making pools for swaps and other DeFi products. CAKE should be assessed as an exchange token, not as a base-layer network. The available snapshot does not record PancakeSwap's fee, revenue, DEX volume, audits, or code activity, so it cannot establish the protocol's current trading position. It retains broad recognition at search rank forty-three and 260k watchlists, while market-cap rank is ninety-two. The purpose is clear; the operating evidence in this dataset is limited.

filecoin.purpose: A decentralised storage network where storage providers commit capacity and clients pay for storing data; FIL is used for those incentives and for network collateral. It is infrastructure rather than a general-purpose DeFi platform, so storage demand is the central question. The snapshot shows only $2.5M locked and $164k of issued stablecoins, but does record $45k of monthly and $2.3M of annual protocol revenue. Development is broad at twelve commits from 327 contributors in four weeks. That supports an active project, while our metrics still give only an indirect view of storage use.

official-trump.purpose: An official Donald Trump-themed meme token whose value proposition is attention, branding, and trading interest rather than a protocol service. As with other memes, TVL and revenue are not the relevant test. It is exceptionally visible at search rank eight, with 151k watchlists and $340M of daily volume, despite market-cap rank ninety-five. The snapshot has no public repository, audited operating system, or on-chain business metric. Its role is therefore fully explained by its public identity and liquidity; the data does not show a separate utility.

vechain.purpose: An enterprise-oriented blockchain that targets business data and supply-chain applications, with VET used for value transfer and network economics. It competes as a smart-contract platform, though its stated use is closer to business infrastructure than retail DeFi. The measurable chain footprint is very small at $1.2M locked and $10k of stablecoins. Development is active at 26 commits from 37 contributors in four weeks, and the community is large at 388k watchlists. The code activity supports ongoing maintenance, but the snapshot records limited financial activity on the chain.

curve-dao-token.purpose: The governance token of Curve, an automated market maker designed around efficient swaps between similarly priced assets, especially stablecoins. CRV belongs with exchange and liquidity protocols, where fee generation and trading volume would be the decisive evidence. Those figures are absent from this snapshot, as are audits and protocol TVL. The linked contract repository has no commits in the last four weeks, although ten contributors are recorded, which is too narrow to describe the whole project. Curve retains search rank seventy-three and 116k watchlists, but its current operating scale is not measured here.

ether-fi.purpose: The governance token of ether.fi, an Ethereum liquid-staking and restaking protocol. Users deposit ETH through the protocol and receive liquid representations, while ETHFI governs its direction; it is not itself the staked asset. The snapshot records no protocol TVL, revenue, audit, public repository, or staking measure, so it cannot test ether.fi's scale or how its rewards are produced. ETHFI has market-cap rank 102, $48M of daily volume, and 37k watchlists. Its function is documented, but the relevant operating evidence is absent.

pudgy-penguins.purpose: A token attached to the Pudgy Penguins brand and community, not to a base-layer blockchain or a DeFi protocol with measurable cash flows. Its meaningful segment is attention-driven consumer and meme assets. It has market-cap rank 104 but unusually high visibility at search rank fifteen, 145k watchlists, and $210M of daily volume. The snapshot contains no public repository, TVL, protocol revenue, or audit record, so it cannot show an operating network behind the brand. The data supports strong recognition and liquidity, not a technical utility claim.

aptos.purpose: A smart-contract layer-one built around the Move language and parallel transaction execution, with APT used for fees, staking, and governance. It competes with newer high-throughput platforms. Its on-chain footprint is modest but real: $55M locked, $1.1B of stablecoins issued, and $88k of monthly protocol revenue. The snapshot has no linked repository, so development is not measured despite the chain's technical focus. At market-cap rank 105, it has search rank eighty-one and 139k watchlists, indicating attention somewhat ahead of its capitalisation standing.

aerodrome-finance.purpose: The governance and incentive token of Aerodrome, a decentralised exchange and liquidity marketplace on Base. Liquidity providers and voters direct incentives between trading pools, so exchange fees and volume would be the relevant proof of its role. This snapshot records none of those protocol measures, nor a public repository or audit record. AERO nonetheless has market-cap rank 107, search rank eighty-six, 83k watchlists, and $34M of daily token volume. The description establishes its function, while the dataset cannot assess the exchange's actual operating scale.

blockstack.purpose: A Bitcoin-adjacent smart-contract network where Stacks transactions settle through Bitcoin and STX pays for execution. Its chain remains small, with $85M locked and $12M of stablecoins at market-cap rank 108. Search rank forty-one and 102k watchlists show recognition, but the snapshot has no public development signal or protocol revenue.

bianrensheng.purpose: A meme token with no documented protocol function in the available data. Its relevant evidence is attention and liquidity: it ranks 109 by market capitalisation but only 987th in search interest, with 2k watchlists and $4.7M daily volume. There is no repository, TVL, revenue, audit, or project description to support a broader claim.

injective-protocol.purpose: A layer-one network focused on on-chain financial markets, where INJ supports staking, governance, and fees.
